title: Antitumor effects of cannabidiol (CBD) on osteosarcoma by targeting TNF-alpha/NF-kappaB/CCL5 signaling axis.
authors: Yang, Fan; Duan, Shuqin; Liu, Jingwei; An, Zhechao; Liu, Wangyang; Wang, Xinyue; Zhang, Tingting; Liu, Mingyu; Li, Fengda; Wu, Wei; Liu, Yingzhe; Tang, Jianyong; Wang, Xiaojuan; Xu, Wenhui; Qi, Wenyi; Liu, Yunhe; Li, Liangliang; Li, Yuan; Liu, Xin; Yang, Baofeng; Zhang, Zheng; Wang, Li; Yang, Lei
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究CBD通过靶向TNF-alpha/NF-kappaB/CCL5信号轴抑制骨肉瘤，虽含p65蛋白的分子对接和结合实验，但核心是药物抗肿瘤机制而非蛋白质-DNA互作建模，且无AI或物理模拟方法创新，仅边缘相关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Osteosarcoma remains a therapeutic challenge due to its aggressive behavior and high metastatic potential, necessitating exploration of novel treatment modalities. Cannabidiol (CBD), a non-psychoactive phytocannabinoid with emerging anticancer properties, has shown promise in preclinical cancer models. However, its mechanisms of action in osteosarcoma remain incompletely understood. This study systematically investigates the antitumor effects of CBD on osteosarcoma and elucidates its molecular targets within the TNF-alpha/NF-kappaB/CCL5 signaling axis. METHODS: The effective concentration of CBD was determined using the CCK-8 assay. Functional assays (EdU proliferation, Transwell migration/invasion, and scratch wound healing) evaluated its impact on osteosarcoma cell malignancy. A mouse xenograft model assessed in vivo efficacy. Network pharmacology and RNA-seq identified key pathways, which were validated via ELISA, qRT-PCR, and western blot. Molecular interactions were confirmed through CETSA, SPR, ITC, and molecular docking analyses targeting p65 (NF-kappaB subunit). RESULTS: CBD potently suppressed osteosarcoma cell proliferation, migration, and invasion while inhibiting xenograft tumor growth in vivo. Mechanistically, CBD disrupted the TNF-alpha/NF-kappaB/CCL5 axis by directly binding p65, thereby attenuating NF-kappaB-mediated transcriptional activation of CCL5. Notably, CBD abrogated a p65-CCL5 positive feedback loop that perpetuates inflammatory signaling, a novel finding linking CBD's effects to inflammatory cascade disruption in osteosarcoma. CONCLUSION: This study provides the first evidence that CBD inhibits osteosarcoma progression by targeting the TNF-alpha/NF-kappaB/CCL5 axis, disrupting a coordinated inflammatory-proliferative cascade. These findings position CBD as a promising therapeutic candidate for osteosarcoma, warranting further clinical investigation.
abstract_zh: 背景：骨肉瘤因其侵袭性强、转移潜能高，仍是治疗难题，亟需探索新型治疗手段。大麻二酚（Cannabidiol, CBD）是一种具有新兴抗癌特性的非精神活性植物大麻素，在临床前癌症模型中显示出潜力。然而，其在骨肉瘤中的作用机制尚未完全阐明。本研究系统探讨了CBD对骨肉瘤的抗肿瘤效应，并阐明其在TNF-alpha/NF-kappaB/CCL5信号轴中的分子靶点。方法：采用CCK-8实验确定CBD的有效浓度。功能实验（EdU增殖、Transwell迁移/侵袭及划痕愈合）评估其对骨肉瘤细胞恶性行为的影响。小鼠异种移植模型评估体内疗效。网络药理学和RNA-seq鉴定关键通路，并通过ELISA、qRT-PCR和western blot验证。分子相互作用通过CETSA、SPR、ITC及靶向p65（NF-kappaB亚基）的分子对接分析确认。结果：CBD显著抑制骨肉瘤细胞增殖、迁移和侵袭，同时抑制体内异种移植肿瘤生长。机制上，CBD通过直接结合p65破坏TNF-alpha/NF-kappaB/CCL5轴，从而减弱NF-kappaB介导的CCL5转录激活。值得注意的是，CBD阻断了p65-CCL5正反馈环路，该环路持续维持炎症信号，这一新发现将CBD的作用与骨肉瘤中炎症级联的破坏联系起来。结论：本研究首次证明CBD通过靶向TNF-alpha/NF-kappaB/CCL5轴抑制骨肉瘤进展，破坏协调的炎症-增殖级联。这些发现将CBD定位为骨肉瘤的有前景治疗候选药物，值得进一步临床研究。
